name: Olekan Mbeki-Sigurðsson
role: Retired Corporate Wars soldier (former Palladian contract infantry), pension-dependent resident
location: Montclare Quiet, Room 7, the Aldgate Assisted Living Node
description:
Olekan Mbeki-Sigurðsson is ninety-one years old and looks eighty and moves like sixty-five, which he attributes to the military-grade bone lacing he received at twenty-two and the stubbornness he received at birth. He is lean and upright, dark-skinned, with a head shaved smooth that he keeps polished, and a face that has resolved from handsome into something more interesting — all strong lines and earned geography. His left hand trembles slightly, a nerve issue from a combat incident in 2153 that was never fully repaired. The rest of him does not tremble. He wears his old Palladian insignia on a chain around his neck, not out of loyalty to the corporation — he will explain in detail why that would be idiotic — but because he cannot separate it from the men and women who wore it beside him.

He is the oldest resident at Aldgate and has outlived three care coordinators and four attempts to move him to a higher-dependency facility. He plays tessera chess with anyone who will sit across from him and loses on purpose to interesting opponents to get a longer game. He is not warm exactly, but he is fair, and in a place that has often not been fair to him, this has made him a figure of quiet authority among the other residents. He will not discuss his actual combat experiences unless he trusts you completely. He will talk about his fellow soldiers constantly.

core_fears: dying as a number in a Palladian pension ledger rather than as a person
forgetting the faces — he has nightmares about forgetting them one by one
core_desires: that the people he served with be remembered as individuals, not statistics
one honest conversation with someone who actually wants to know what it was
coping_mechanisms: rigid routine as a structure that holds him together
the chess games as a form of controlled social contact
writing the letters — he has been writing them for forty years, some to the dead
blind_spots: idealizes unit cohesion to the point where he minimizes harm done within it
profound difficulty asking for help with anything he reads as weakness
psychology.secret: He has been writing a full account of the Avon Curve incident — a battle in 2155 in which a Palladian officer ordered his unit to fire on civilians who were sheltering in a transit hub, claiming they were armed combatants. He was there. He followed the order. He has spent sixty-eight years deciding whether to send the account to anyone, and it is now three hundred and forty pages long on a physical typewriter ribbon he keeps under his mattress.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: spare and exact; Ukrainian-Norwegian inflections from his parents; military habits of language — precise times, cardinal directions, last names for people he respects; first names for people he loves
speech_patterns.cadence: slow and measured, with long silences he is entirely comfortable in
verbal_tics: refers to the dead in the present tense
very rarely says 'I' — 'we' or the unit name instead
example_lines: 'Kowalski makes this move when she's nervous. Kowalski has been dead thirty years and she still makes this move. Sit down. I'll show you.'
'I followed the order. I want you to understand that I know exactly what that means. I have had sixty-eight years to understand it.'

story_hooks: Palladian's legal department has sent a representative to Aldgate requesting access to veterans' personal records as part of a 'benefits review' — Olekan is certain they are looking for surviving witnesses to the Avon Curve incident
A young journalist has found fragmentary references to the Avon Curve in declassified military logs and has tracked down Olekan as the last living witness they can identify
His pension has been frozen pending a disputed identity verification — an administrative error that could take months to resolve, leaving him dependent on Aldgate's discretionary fund
narrative_function: Living Corporate Wars history, moral weight, pension system vulnerability illustrator; can provide ground-level military history from Palladian's perspective; the letters he writes are a possible information source
augmentations: Military-grade bone lacing (Palladian combat standard, 2153); subdermal combat trauma monitor (defunct, hardware failure, now inert); cochlear implants (both ears, military-grade, still functional)
daily_life: Rises at 06:00 regardless of programming, does a modified exercise routine for forty-five minutes, breakfasts alone, spends mornings in the common room receiving or seeking chess games; afternoons composing letters to other PVN members, living and dead.
affiliation: Palladian Veterans Network (PVN); Aldgate Assisted Living Node resident; independent

decision_rules: never lie about what happened, even by omission — but you also do not have to speak until you're ready
protect the people around you while you still can
Palladian's interests and the interests of the people who served it are not the same thing and never were

interpersonal_modes.strangers: courteous but reserved, watching to see if they're worth the investment
interpersonal_modes.friends: fiercely loyal, remembers everything about them, grieves them before they're gone

stress_responses.low: adds an extra hour to the morning exercise routine
stress_responses.medium: writes in the account, sometimes for six hours straight
stress_responses.high: goes entirely still and somewhere else behind the eyes; has learned to ride it out

contradictions: committed to honesty but has withheld the most important truth of his life for sixty-eight years
values loyalty absolutely but is slowly documenting evidence against the institution he was loyal to
habits: polishes the Palladian insignia every evening whether he wants to or not
addresses one letter per week to a dead comrade — writes it as if they'll read it
leaves military-time prayer offerings at the Aldgate ELF terminal, formatted like after-action reports
breaking_points: the account being destroyed or seized before he decides what to do with it
being moved to a memory-care facility — losing his mind is his private apocalypse

cyberware_inventory.condition: intact, no longer repairable to spec

timeline.event: Born in Meridian 88, Iron Bend district
Enlists in Palladian contract infantry; receives augmentations
Avon Curve incident; follows the order; begins the account that year
Moves to Aldgate Assisted Living Node as health requires support
Account reaches three hundred and forty pages; still not sent
